newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BELCHATOW POWER PLANT EYES FOUR INVESTORS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BELCHATOW POWER PLANT EYES FOUR INVESTORS.

text.p: Four international energy firms are interested in investing in a new $1 billion, 800 megawatt, lignite power plant Belchatow 2, the new firm's chief said on Tuesday.

Zbigniew Zakrzewski told Reuters during an energy industry conference that state-owned Elektrownia Belchatow, which now owns 100 percent of Belchatow 2, planned to offer up to 49 percent of the new company to foreign investors.
He said Belchatow, in central Poland, had been approached by U.S. firms Southern Electric and Community Energy Alternatives Inc, Japan's Marubeni Corp and Sweden's Wattenfall.
"Those four companies have contacted us and are interested in equity investment in Belchatow 2," Zakrzewski said.
He said the company planned to pick equity investors by the end of this year.
Zakrzewski said that to reduce the risk for investors the new company would seek to secure long-term energy supply contracts as well as lignite supplies for the plant.

He said that under a preliminary plan $200 million of investment would be financed through the new firm's new capital while the remaining $800 million would be covered by a syndicated loan or debt issues.

In 1995 Belchatow signed a letter of intent with state-owned Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA, now a member of Bank Pekao SA group, under which PBG would arrange the financing for the $1 billion project.
